newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to develop export promotion programme.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to develop export promotion programme.

text.p: Brazil's Foreign Trade Council will develop during 1997 a package of measures to boost exports, said the council's executive secretary, Frederico Alvarez.

Alvarez told reporters after a regular meeting of the body that the aim was to bring all government export promotion initiatives under a single roof and devise long-term incentives for overseas sales.
"It is necessary to increase the participation of Brazilian exports in international trade and also local gross domestic product," he said.
The government Tuesday announced a record trade deficit in 1996 of $5.539 billion. Exports grew only 2.67 percent, while imports jumped 6.88 percent over 1995.

Brasilia has already taken some steps to help exports -- freeing raw materials and some semi-manufactureds from export tax, reviving an export insurance agency and setting up some special credit lines.
Alvarez said the government also wanted to increase the numbers of Brazilian firms exporting -- currently only about 0.5 percent of the total -- and encourage added value exports.
The programme would also involve steps to reduce the cost of doing business in Brazil, the so-called Brazil Cost, additional credit lines and promotional campaigns and research into demand abroad.

Alvarez said the council would analyze a list of 58 suggestions from the National Industry Confederation (CNI) and a report by the Ministry of Industry and Commerce that recommended special attention be paid to 15 key industrial sectors.
